name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.137.0 — The build driver's gate now sees the files the build itself created: immediately before spawning the gate child, runGate() adds every untracked, non-ignored File Plan path to the index with intent-to-add (git add -N), so an index-reading host check (a size baseline, a duplication scan, a file manifest) counts a newly created file's real on-disk bytes at build time instead of only after the checkpoint commit made it tracked, at review. The staging is bounded to the spec's own File Plan paths — an out-of-plan creation stays untracked and remains scope-reconcile's finding at commit — and the staged entries are never reverted by the driver, surviving every repair round and the checkpoint commit that consumes them. A File Plan path a host's .gitignore hides is warned about and skipped rather than refused; a failed staging call is a fail-closed refusal (exit 2, no gate child spawned, no gateRuns entry recorded) rather than a gate that ran blind. This is the driver's only index write — every other git call it makes stays a read — and specs/20260901/01-build-driver.md D12's absolute 'never runs a git write' is narrowed accordingly under docs/adr/0015, with spec/commands/build.md's matching Rules clause narrowed in the same build. 7.136.0 — Hosts can now declare an optional postGateCommand in .claude/spec.config.json: after the scoped build gate passes, spec-build-driver.js chains this command into the same gate run at integration and on every repair round, so a build that passes its own test directories but breaks a repo-wide pin (a version bump, a size ratchet, a read-load budget, a byte-for-byte config pin) is repaired by the build's own workers instead of bouncing red at review. The literal {testCommand} inside postGateCommand substitutes the host's testCommand string; a red post-gate lands REPAIR with a new post-gate: line naming the command in the REPAIR step body, and the build ledger's gate object records whether a post-gate was declared. A host with no such key runs byte-for-byte what it ran before; review's suite leg and the shared gate resolver are unchanged. This repo now declares {testCommand} as its own post-gate. 7.135.0 — The mocks seed now names the client's real records and the two dense screens the theme pick judges every candidate on (ADR-0013): the seed's `## Records` section names one JSON file of at least three real records per entity, refused missing/short/invented at seed-done (and on a cold host the refusal still names the remedy with a literal `<entity>` placeholder); `## Dense screens` accepts one or two declared labels (the singular `## Dense screen` heading still parses for hosts seeded earlier); and journey-drawn now warns per screen and refuses per journey when no drawn screen carries a value from those records, so a journey never reaches the client on placeholder data.
